claims.claim: High Quality Solar Panels, Inverters, Lithium & Tubular Batteries, Charge...
claims.evidence: Seller text mentions multiple product types, but the photos only show a solar panel; no inverter/battery/charger is shown.

risks.risk: Panel wattage/efficiency rating is unknown (price depends heavily on watt class like 100W/150W/200W+).
risks.proof: A clear close-up photo of the panel’s label/specs (brand, model, Pmax in W, Voc, Isc, serial number) on the back or frame.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a generic mid/low-watt solar panel with unknown performance.

risks.risk: Condition of the glass/cells is uncertain due to visible smudges/marks; could be dust or could be micro-cracks/impact damage.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the cell grid under direct light plus a photo of the panel from the side to check for cracks; ideally an IR/flash test report.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not guaranteed (worst case: possible damage/underperformance).

risks.risk: Electrical working status is unknown (no test results shown).
risks.proof: A multimeter/IV curve test screenshot or a simple on-site power test showing output under sun (or a flash-test report).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not working/unknown performance until tested.

risks.risk: Compatibility/installation details unknown (connector type, cable length, junction box condition).
risks.proof: Photo of the junction box and connectors (MC4 type or other), plus close-up of cable condition and polarity markings.
risks.if_unproven: Priced assuming standard connectors but with no guarantee; buyer may need extra parts.

proof_requests: Clear photo of the panel nameplate/spec label (brand/model, Pmax in W, Voc, Isc, serial number).
Close-up of the junction box and connector type (e.g., MC4) and cable condition.
Photo(s) showing the glass/cell area clearly (no glare) to confirm there are no cracks.
Any test proof: IV curve/flash test report or a measured output under sun.
response.reason: From the photos, this appears to be a solar panel, but the key pricing drivers (wattage/spec label, condition of cells, and whether it’s working) are not readable or proven. Without those, a reliable worst-case price can’t be set.
